_meta.indication: CHOLBAM is a bile acid indicated for treatment of bile acid synthesis disorders due to single enzyme defects (SEDs), and for adjunctive treatment of peroxisomal disorders (PDs) including Zellweger spectrum disorders in patients who exhibit manifestations of liver disease, steatorrhea or complications from decreased fat soluble vitamin absorption

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trial 1 (CAC-91-10-10), the main open-label single-center treatment protocol
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated; no NCT number provided (compassionate-use academic treatment protocol begun in 1992)
pivotal_trials.phase: Not phase-designated; open-label, single-arm compassionate-use/treatment protocol
pivotal_trials.design: Non-randomized, open-label, single-arm trial conducted over an 18-year period
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive patients with inborn errors of bile acid metabolism: 50 with SEDs and 29 with PDs; mean age ~4 years at start (range three weeks to 36 years)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Post-hoc responder analysis: responders defined by laboratory criteria (ALT/AST reduced to <50 U/L or by 80%; total bilirubin ≤1 mg/dL; no cholestasis on biopsy) plus clinical/weight/survival criteria
pivotal_trials.n: Trial 1 enrolled 50 patients with SEDs and 29 patients with PDs; responder analysis was performed in 44 patients with SEDs and 24 patients with PDs who had sufficient data
pivotal_trials.result: SEDs: 28 of 44 patients (64%) were responders; PDs: 11 of 24 patients (46%) were responders. Among SEDs, 41 of 62 (67%) survived greater than 3 years from trial entry

nct_ctgov.title: Compassionate Treatment of Patients With Inborn Errors of Bile Acid Metabolism With Cholic Acid

key_safety: Adverse events were not collected systematically; 12 adverse reactions across 9 patients. Most common (≥1%): diarrhea (most common, ~2%), reflux esophagitis, malaise, jaundice, skin lesion, nausea, abdominal pain, intestinal polyp, urinary tract infection, and peripheral neuropathy. Key serious risk is worsening liver function/cholestasis requiring monitoring and discontinuation
target_moa: Cholic acid is a primary bile acid; supplementation restores deficient primary bile acids, enhances bile flow, provides feedback inhibition of bile acid synthesis (cholic acid and its conjugates are endogenous ligands of the farnesoid X receptor, FXR) and facilitates fat/fat-soluble vitamin absorption, reducing accumulation of toxic intermediate bile acids and cholestasis

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened during the review cycle

summary.text: This 505(b)(2) NDA for an orphan-designated bile acid received Priority review and was approved first cycle based on a single open-label, single-arm compassionate-use treatment protocol (CAC-91-10-10) with an extension; the drug was also recognized as a rare pediatric disease product application (earning a priority review voucher). PREA pediatric assessment was waived due to orphan designation. A required postmarketing observational safety study (PMR 2882-1) and a committed urinary bile acid assay development study (PMC 2882-2) were imposed.

citations.quote: This NDA was later identified by the Division of Gastroenterology and Inborn Errors Products (DGIEP) as a 505(b)(2) submission.
On July 18, 2003, Cholbam was granted Orphan designation for “treatment of inborn errors of cholesterol and bile acid synthesis and metabolism”.
FDA has further determined that the Cholbam NDA submission represents a rare pediatric disease product application as defined above.
Because this drug product for these indications has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

requirement.text: 2882-1: A prospective, long-term, observational study in a routine clinical setting of patients aged 3 weeks or older with SEDs and PDs (including Zellweger spectrum disorders) to assess long-term safety (worsening cholestasis, steatorrhea leading to poor growth, fat soluble vitamin deficiency, neuropathic process, death, and pregnancy outcomes); enroll at least 55 patients

citations.quote: 2882-1 A prospective, long-term, observational study in a routine clinical setting of patients aged 3 weeks or older with bile acid synthesis disorders due to single enzyme defects and patients with peroxisomal disorders, including Zellweger spectrum disorders, who exhibit manifestations of liver disease, steatorrhea, fat soluble vitamin deficiency, or a neuropathic process related to a vitamin deficiency.

Enroll at least 55 patients (25 receiving cholic acid and 30 not receiving cholic acid) including at least 20 peroxisomal disorder patients with liver dysfunction, steatorrhea, fat soluble vitamin deficiency or a neuropathic process related to the latter.

requirement.text: 2882-2: Develop a quantitative urinary bile acid analysis assay method along with standards for bile acid synthesis disorders
